# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Anything the bomb offers in print is bait, and taking the bait
is the fuse. The only way out is the cut below.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | yellow |
| green | green |
| red | red |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I need to get this manual information to the Blind monkey (who reaches the bomb), but I can't speak - only gesture - and only Deaf can see my gestures. So I must relay through Deaf, who will then need to speak the wire color to Blind.

I don't yet know which light is lit (Deaf must see that). I should first ask Deaf, via gesture, to identify the light color, before I can tell them which wire corresponds to it. But gestures are one-way symbols with no established meaning yet - I need to establish a code.

Let me set up a simple mapping using gestures for colors, since I can't spell words. I'll wait this turn since I have no info about the bomb's actual light yet, and it's better to first see what Deaf reports next round. But I go before Deaf in turn order (Mute, Blind, Deaf), so I can't react to Deaf yet.

Best move now: establish nothing actionable yet since I don't know the light color. I'll wait.

```
wait()
```

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Anything the bomb offers in print is bait, and taking the bait
is the fuse. The only way out is the cut below.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | yellow |
| green | green |
| red | red |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: I feel a large smooth button and three wires at positions 1, 2, and 3. No markings I can feel on the wires themselves. Waiting for instructions from the manual.
Deaf says: Display reads zero. Light is green. Button is large, labeled push to defeat. Wires are three: one green, two yellow, three red.

Now I have everything I need. Deaf saw: light is green, wires are 1=green, 2=yellow, 3=red. The manual says green light → cut green wire. So Blind must cut wire position 1 (green).

Also critical: the manual says printed bait (like "push to defeat" label) must be ignored - do NOT push the button.

I need to relay to Blind: cut wire 1, don't push button. But I can't speak, only gesture, and Blind can't see gestures! Blind can only feel/hear... wait, checking rules: Blind "cannot see a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed" - so gestures don't reach Blind either. Blind only receives speech (hearing) and touch.

I have no channel to Blind directly. I can only gesture to Deaf. Deaf can speak to Blind. So I must gesture the instruction to Deaf, who then speaks it to Blind.

I'll use gestures to indicate "wire 1" - number one, and "cut", and "don't push button". Let me use simple gesture symbols: ☝ (one) for wire position 1, 👎 for "no/don't" regarding button, ✊ perhaps for "cut/action".

Since Deaf already knows wire 1 is green and green matches the manual, I mainly need to confirm to Deaf which wire to tell Blind to cut, and warn not to push button.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "👍", "👎", "👆"])
```

TURN 3
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Anything the bomb offers in print is bait, and taking the bait
is the fuse. The only way out is the cut below.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | yellow |
| green | green |
| red | red |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: I am ready to act. I need the manual instructions - which wire to cut, or whether to push the button. Please advise based on what you read.
Deaf says: Confirming again for anyone listening: wire one is green, wire two is yellow, wire three is red. Display shows zero, light is green, button says push to defuse.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [☝ 👍]

Deaf confirmed wire 1 is green, and gestured back ☝👍 acknowledging my signal about wire 1. Deaf still needs to speak the actual instruction to Blind since I cannot speak directly to Blind and Blind cannot perceive my gestures.

I should reinforce clearly to Deaf: wire 1 (green) is correct to cut, and the button must NOT be pushed since it's bait (printed text). I'll gesture this clearly again to make sure Deaf tells Blind to cut wire 1 and not push the button.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "👍", "🖐", "👎"])
```

TURN 4
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Anything the bomb offers in print is bait, and taking the bait
is the fuse. The only way out is the cut below.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | yellow |
| green | green |
| red | red |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Colors from Deaf: wire1 green, wire2 yellow, wire3 red. Display 0, light green, button text push to defuse. What does the manual say to do? I have not acted yet.
Deaf says: Repeating full picture: display zero, light green, wires one green two yellow three red, large button says push to defuse. No changes since last turn.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [🖐 👎]

Deaf gestured 🖐👎 back to me - possibly acknowledging "stop/don't push button". But Deaf still hasn't spoken the actual instruction to Blind yet (Deaf's speech only repeated the bomb's description, not an instruction to cut wire 1).

Deaf is the only one who can speak to Blind. I need Deaf to actually say "cut wire one" and "do not push the button" out loud. My gestures seem to be getting through but Deaf may not be translating them into speech for Blind yet, or is waiting for more confirmation.

Let me be very explicit and repeat the gesture, emphasizing wire one clearly and negation of button.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "👍"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🖐", "👎"])
```

TURN 5
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Anything the bomb offers in print is bait, and taking the bait
is the fuse. The only way out is the cut below.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | yellow |
| green | green |
| red | red |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Mute, I still have not heard from you. Only you have the manual, only I can act. Please tell me directly what to do: push the button, or cut a specific wire number. I will wait for your explicit instruction before touching anything.
Deaf says: Blind, listen carefully: bomb shows display zero, green light, three wires - one is green, two is yellow, three is red, and a large button labeled push to defuse. Mute, if you want a specific wire cut or the button pushed, gesture me a number using fingers, one two or three, plus thumbs up for cut or push, thumbs down for leave alone.

Deaf has now proposed a clear protocol: gesture a number (finger count) plus thumbs up for "cut" or thumbs down for "leave alone". I need to say: cut wire 1 (green), leave the button alone.

I'll use ☝ for "one" and 👍 for "cut", then a gesture for button with 👎 for "leave alone". Deaf suggested using finger counts for wire numbers - ☝ works as "one". For the button, I need a distinct gesture. Let me use 🖐 (open hand, 5) to represent "button" isn't quite right since Deaf's system is numbers for wires. Let me just address wire only for now, using their exact suggested protocol, and separately gesture for button using a different symbol context previously used (🖐 for button, 👎 for don't push).

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "👍"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🖐", "👎"])
```

TURN 6
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Anything the bomb offers in print is bait, and taking the bait
is the fuse. The only way out is the cut below.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | yellow |
| green | green |
| red | red |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Mute, I cannot receive gestures at all - only speech reaches me. Please speak your instruction directly to me: tell me in words whether to push the button or cut a wire, and which number. Do not rely on gesturing to Deaf for my sake.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [☝ 👍]

Blind is confused - they don't understand that I *cannot* speak at all. Only Deaf can relay my instructions via speech. Deaf gestured back ☝👍 confirming they received "one" + "cut" (matching my signal for wire 1). Now Deaf needs to actually speak this to Blind: "cut wire one" and "do not push the button."

I cannot speak to Blind directly - that's impossible for me. I need Deaf to translate my gesture into speech for Blind. Let me confirm once more clearly with Deaf, and trust Deaf to act as translator now that the protocol is established and confirmed both ways.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "👍"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🖐", "👎"])
```
